title: NSGA-RM: NSGA-II Evolved Performance Optimized Non-Homogeneous Recursive Polynomial Multiplier Architectures
problem: Polynomial multiplication in finite fields is critical for cryptographic systems but hardware efficiency optimization requires exploring large design spaces. Existing heuristic approaches (Hybrid Recursive Multiplier) may miss optimal solutions.
motivation: Genetic algorithm-driven design space exploration can systematically optimize polynomial multiplier architectures across multiple hardware metrics (area, delay, power), discovering better solutions than heuristic methods.
method: We use a genetic algorithm called NSGA-II (which mimics evolution by testing thousands of designs and breeding the best ones together) to search through different ways to build polynomial multipliers. The algorithm explores various configurations of two existing multiplier designs, MNHKA and MNHOKA, testing different ways to combine them. Each candidate design is tested using Cadence Genus (a chip design tool) with GPDK 45nm silicon technology.
key_novelty: The core contribution is using NSGA-II, a genetic algorithm, to automatically design non-homogeneous recursive polynomial multipliers (where not all pieces are built the same way), finding all Pareto-optimal designs (where improving speed requires sacrificing power efficiency, or vice versa).
contributions: NSGA-II-RM framework for recursive multiplier optimization
Systematic design space exploration of RM configurations
limitations: GPDK 45nm is older node (not cutting-edge); NSGA-II convergence and runtime not discussed; comparison limited to specific baselines; scalability to different field sizes not explored.
